calls.head: Vasilevskiy’s hold on the Islanders won’t last
calls.body: Since 2023-24, Vasilevskiy has been a wall against the Islanders, well above his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if the Islanders finally get to him.

TBL.head: We gave Tampa Bay a 64% chance, and they delivered.

surprises.head: The Islanders’ power play came alive
surprises.body: The Islanders have had one of the league’s least effective power plays for years, and Tampa Bay kills penalties better than most. Not tonight: the Islanders’ power play created 16.2 expected goals per 60, against their usual 6.8 (about 6.4 against Tampa Bay) and a league average of 7.6. A team strays this far about once every 40 games.

story.head: Hagel lights the lamp for a hat trick
paras: Jake Guentzel opened the scoring for the Lightning early in the first, and Brandon Hagel made it 2-0 late in the period. It was a busy second period. Tony DeAngelo got the Islanders on the board early in the period. Guentzel scored again on the power play a minute and a half later to make it 3-1 for the Lightning. Scott Sabourin and Logan Stanley squared off midway through the second, and Jean-Gabriel Pageau pulled the Isles within one midway through the period. Brayden Schenn tied it up on the power play with just 7 seconds left in the period, but they didn’t score again. Hagel scored his second of the night with less than two minutes left to put the Lightning ahead for good. Hagel completed his hat trick into the empty net with less than two minutes left.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Andrei Vasilevskiy made 20 saves for the Lightning, and Ilya Sorokin stopped 21 of 25. By our Swing measure, Matthew Schaefer had the best night of anyone, even in a loss and with Hagel’s hat trick in the game. The Lightning moved to 4-1-0, and the Islanders fell to 2-3-0.

items.text: Four straight wins for the Lightning.
Nikita Kucherov has a point in every game this season.
Jean-Gabriel Pageau scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 9.
With Emil Lilleberg out, Max Crozier took his spot and had two assists.
